summary:
AstroBlocks – Build Before Disaster! is a Tetris-inspired educational space exploration game designed to make space science intuitive, interactive and accessible to younger audiences.

The game features 16 stages representing real-world locations and missions inspired by actual space exploration events, three of which have been scientifically calibrated to date: the International Space Station (ISS), the Sea of Tranquility (Moon), and Jezero Crater (Mars). We integrated datasets provided within the challenge and extended our research to additional NASA scientific resources.

NASA DONKI space weather observations and RadLab radiation measurements were incorporated into historical environmental monitoring. NASA Mars Trek and MOLA elevation data informed geographical visualisation, terrain representation and construction requirements, while Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) research informed plant-growth mechanics and educational activities.

Beyond the challenge datasets, we incorporated astronaut oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production data, Martian dust opacity measurements, Perseverance rock-sampling records, Ingenuity aerial imagery and Apollo mission archives.

AstroBlocks addresses the challenge by transforming NASA's scientific data and mission records into an interactive learning experience, encouraging curiosity, scientific literacy, problem-solving and an interest in space exploration among younger audiences.
details:
Project Overview

AstroBlocks – Build Before Disaster! is an interactive, Tetris-inspired educational game that combines space exploration, habitat construction, resource management and scientific discovery. It is designed primarily for younger audiences to explore the scientific and engineering challenges associated with space exploration through gameplay.



How It Works

The game features 16 stages representing real-world locations and missions inspired by actual space exploration events, with three currently developed and tested in greater detail: the International Space Station (ISS), the Sea of Tranquility and Jezero Crater.

Players use a Tetris-inspired puzzle to acquire construction materials and assemble functional infrastructure within simulated space environments. As players progress, their installations become visible and interactive, including solar panels, batteries, oxygen supply systems, greenhouses and scientific equipment.

AstroBlocks offers two interchangeable gameplay modes: Puzzle + Crew Mode and Astronaut Only Mode. Players can either combine puzzle-based resource acquisition with astronaut-controlled construction or collect materials and assemble infrastructure directly within the simulated environment without playing Tetris. This flexibility was aimed at accommodating different gameplay preferences and learning styles while preserving the scientific and educational objectives.

Beyond habitat construction, players can undertake scientific expeditions, operate rovers, conduct aerial surveys, collect geological samples and experience mission-inspired cinematic sequences. An integrated Learn Bot provides educational explanations, gameplay guidance and mission objectives.


Scientific Data Integration

I integrated datasets provided within the challenge and extended our research to additional NASA scientific resources, including:

  • NASA DONKI: Historical space weather observations.
  • NASA RadLab: Historical radiation measurements aboard the ISS.
  • NASA Mars Trek and MOLA: Geographical visualisation, elevation profiles and terrain-informed construction mechanics.
  • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR): Space-based plant research and greenhouse learning activities.
  • NASA BVAD: Astronaut oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production.
  • NASA MEDA: Martian atmospheric dust opacity and its simulated influence on solar energy availability.
  • NASA mission archives: Perseverance rock-sampling records, Ingenuity aerial imagery and Apollo mission photographs.

Scientific observations are incorporated into simplified educational models, with clear distinctions between real-world data and simulated scenarios.

Tools and Technologies

AstroBlocks was developed using HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas and WebGL-based visualisations. Python was used for data preparation, processing and build automation, while Node.js and automated browser testing supported functionality assessment.

The application is designed for offline browser-based gameplay, with keyboard and touchscreen controls to improve accessibility. Development was supported by AI-assisted coding and iterative testing.

Creativity and Intended Impact

The project's creativity lies in transforming a familiar puzzle mechanic into a meaningful space exploration experience, where solving puzzles produces tangible changes within an interactive environment.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, age-appropriate learning, accessibility, gameplay duration, visual engagement, intuitive navigation and the distinction between scientific evidence and fictional simulations.

Ultimately, AstroBlocks aims to strengthen scientific literacy, curiosity, critical thinking and problem-solving, while inspiring younger generations to explore STEM disciplines and the possibilities of future space exploration.
